title: Vector-unit billing pilot for embeddings & rerank — dynamic batch discounts and enterprise QSA pack
creator: Marisa Chen
description:
Goal: Run a controlled pilot that moves embeddings and reranking usage to a unitized 'vector-unit' pricing model with a dynamic batch-discount mechanic. Deliver an enterprise-grade QSA artifacts pack (answers + evidence) so sales/legal can include the pilot terms in SOWs.

Scope:
- Pricing model: introduce vector-unit base price + graduated batch-discount curve (volume breakpoints and session-level batching).
- Billing prototype: invoice simulation job + per-customer cost report for pilot customers.
- UX/Docs: single-page pricing explainer, migration notes, and a QuickStart for partners.
- QSA pack: completed questionnaire responses, dataflow diagrams, KMS/HSM evidence notes, and audit log extracts for two sample customers.

Success metrics (pilot criteria):
- Economics: median per-vector unit cost falls within target band for 3 pilot customers (target: $0.0009–$0.0016 per vector after batching).
- Adoption: 2 pilot enterprise accounts sign off on pilot SLA and pricing for at least one month.
- Accuracy: no detectable increase in rerank quality regressions (A/B vs baseline, <1% drift).
- Billing accuracy: invoice simulation error <0.5% vs ground-truth token accounting.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Pricing calculus and discount curve documented and approved by revenue & finance.
2) Invoice simulator producing customer-level reports and CSV exports.
3) QSA pack drafted and validated by security/infra; at least one dry run with legal.
4) Pilot contract template and SOW language ready for sales (legal-approved).
5) Post-pilot recommendation (go/no-go + rollout plan) and a migration path for self-serve customers.

Deliverables:
- pricing-playbook/vector-unit-pricing.md (confluence link placeholder)
- invoice-sim job + sample CSVs in Drive (drive.google.com/drive/folder/placeholder)
- qsa-pack/answers-and-evidence.pdf (attached to ticket)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/292 (billing calc & exports)
- dashboard: billing-sim.pilot (Looker tile) with per-customer unit economics

Stakeholders:
- Product: Marisa Chen (owner), Diego Alvarez (pm lead)
- Finance: Priya Raman (pricing sign-off)
- Legal/Sales Ops: Connor Briggs (SOW)
- Security/Infosec: Elena Marin (QSA owner)
- Engineering: runtime billing (ENG-4210), telemetry (ENG-4356)
- Solutions & AE: Olivia Park (pilot customers)

Risks & mitigations:
- Billing edge cases (e.g., shared sessions across projects) — mitigation: simulator-level dedupe and trace logs.
- Unexpected unit economics for short sequences — mitigation: include sequence-length stratified reports and fallback PS (per-request cap).
- QSA evidence gaps — mitigation: pre-check list and two-week evidence collection window before formal QSA deliverable.

Timeline (high level):
- Week 1 (Mar 10–16): finalize discount curve and finance model; draft QSA checklist.
- Week 2 (Mar 17–23): build invoice simulator + reporting; initial legal review of pilot SOW.
- Week 3 (Mar 24–30): run simulation against historical traffic from 3 candidate customers; create delta reports.
- Week 4 (Mar 31–Apr 6): security dry run and finalize QSA pack; sales dry run of SOW.
- Week 5 (Apr 7–13): onboard pilot customers; begin live telemetry; weekly check-ins.
- Post-pilot (by Apr 30): summarize results and recommend next steps (scale, iterate, or cancel).

Notes on experimentation design:
- Use matched-pair analysis per account: compare baseline pricing vs vector-unit pricing under actual traffic for a 30-day window.
- Track both cost-to-serve (infra) and net revenue per vector to ensure we don't create a negative-margin cohort.
- Expose adjustable parameters (discount slope, batch-window ms) behind a feature flag to test sensitivity without deploy churn.

Required approvals before kickoff:
- Finance sign-off on target price band (Priya Raman)
- Security confirmation that QSA sample evidence is retrievable (Elena Marin)
- Legal sign-off on pilot SOW language (Connor Briggs)

If approved: we will create two follow-up tickets — PM for pilot management (status board, weekly notes) and ENG work items for instrumentation and export hooks.
